--- title: "A tiny rubric for evaluating LLM answers" description: "You don't need a framework to start evaluating model output. A spreadsheet-sized rubric and twenty lines of Python get you surprisingly far." date: 2026-11-02 categories: [AI, Python, evaluation] image: ../../../assets/svg/illustrations/chip.svg jupyter: python3 --- Most teams wait too long to evaluate their LLM features. They're looking for the *right* framework when a small, honest rubric would already tell them most of what they need. ## The loop ```{mermaid} flowchart LR A[Collect 30 real prompts] --> B[Generate answers] B --> C{Score with rubric} C -->|pass| D[Ship] C -->|fail| E[Change prompt or model] E --> B ``` ## The rubric Three criteria, each scored 0–2. Keep it boring, keep it consistent. ::: {#2ed85f68 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd scores = pd.DataFrame({ "variant": ["Baseline", "Baseline", "Baseline", "New prompt", "New prompt", "New prompt"], "criterion": ["Correct", "Grounded", "Concise"] * 2, "score": [1.2, 0.9, 1.6, 1.7, 1.5, 1.4], }) scores.pivot(index="criterion", columns="variant", values="score") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
variant Baseline New prompt
criterion
Concise 1.6 1.4
Correct 1.2 1.7
Grounded 0.9 1.5
``` ::: ::: ## What changed ::: {#cell-fig-rubric .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import matplotlib.pyplot as plt wide = scores.pivot(index="criterion", columns="variant", values="score") ax = wide.plot.bar(rot=0, width=0.7) ax.set_title("The new prompt wins on correctness and grounding") ax.set_xlabel("") ax.set_ylim(0, 2) ax.legend(title="") plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Average rubric score by criterion (0–2).](index_files/figure-html/fig-rubric-output-1.png){#fig-rubric width=980 height=613} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip} ## Rule of thumb If every change "wins", your rubric isn't sensitive enough. Add a harder prompt or two. ::: > Evaluate early, evaluate small, evaluate often.
